title: Graph kernels, PageRank, and power iteration
summary: Prove a graph-kernel construction is positive semidefinite, determine a kernel-parameter range, and compute PageRank as a fixed-point iteration.
objectives: Use feature maps to prove PSD

sourceRefs.role: past-exam graph kernel and PageRank alignment

sections.title: Textbook depth · Kernel PSD by feature map
sections.body: A kernel is positive semidefinite when every finite Gram matrix is PSD. The safest proof pattern is to write $K(G,G')=\langle\Psi(G),\Psi(G')\rangle$ for an explicit or implicit feature map. Sums of valid kernels remain valid because their feature maps can be concatenated.

math.explanation: The quadratic-form test proves PSD directly once the feature map is identified. For graph kernels, coordinates can count node labels, edge patterns, walks, or other substructures.
math.name: Graph-kernel positive-semidefinite proof
math.purpose: Use it to certify a kernel by rewriting its quadratic form as a squared feature-map norm.

sections.title: Assessment bridge · Opposite-edge parameter
sections.body: If a graph-kernel Gram block for two opposite orientations is $[[1,q],[q,1]]$, its eigenvalues are $1+q$ and $1-q$. Positive semidefiniteness therefore requires $-1\le q\le1$. Always derive the range from the actual Gram block stated in the question; do not infer it from a visual intuition about similarity.

math.explanation: Both eigenvalues must be non-negative. The boundary values are PSD but can make the feature representation linearly dependent.
math.name: Graph-kernel eigenvalue condition
math.purpose: Use it to determine the parameter range for which the graph-kernel Gram matrix remains positive semidefinite.

sections.title: Reference depth · PageRank as a fixed point
sections.body: Construct a column- or row-stochastic transition matrix $P$, repair dangling nodes, and apply damping: $r_{t+1}=\alpha P^\top r_t+(1-\alpha)\frac1n\mathbf1$. The stationary ranking is an eigenvector/fixed point normalized to sum to one.

math.explanation: Damping makes the random-surfer chain well behaved even when the raw graph has sinks or disconnected structure. Check the orientation convention: whether vectors are columns or rows changes where the transpose appears.
math.name: PageRank fixed-point equation
math.purpose: Use it to compute or iterate the stationary importance vector while accounting for teleportation.

sections.title: Assessment habit · Matrix orientation and normalization
sections.body: Before multiplying, state whether P is row-stochastic or column-stochastic and whether r is a row or column vector. After each iteration, check non-negativity and that the rank vector sums to one. These checks catch most PageRank arithmetic errors.

examples.title: PSD parameter range
steps: Its eigenvectors are [1,1] and [1,-1], with eigenvalues 1+q and 1-q.
Both are non-negative exactly when q is between -1 and 1 inclusive.
examples.answer: A small Gram eigenvalue is a numerical warning even when the matrix is theoretically PSD.

examples.title: One PageRank update
steps: Start with r0 uniform on n nodes. Multiply by the transition operator to move mass along outgoing links.
Mix $\alpha$ times the propagated mass with (1-$\alpha$) times the uniform teleportation vector.
Verify that the resulting entries remain non-negative and sum to one.
examples.answer: Power iteration is repeated matrix-vector multiplication plus damping; it is not an eigen-decomposition requirement for a small exam calculation.

criticalQuestions.prompt: What makes a kernel proof robust?
criticalQuestions.modelAnswer: Identify a feature map or a PSD Gram block, then show every coefficient quadratic form is a squared norm or has non-negative eigenvalues.

criticalQuestions.prompt: Why can a transpose appear in PageRank?
criticalQuestions.modelAnswer: A row-stochastic matrix propagates row vectors on the right; a column rank vector typically uses the transpose of that transition convention. The mathematics is the same after fixing one orientation.
